title: The Five Fathers: the Lord's descent through five discrete degrees from inmost Divine to the soul at the door of heaven
arc: The teaching traces a single chain of emanation in which Divine love and wisdom proceed from the Father of Greatness through five successive Fathers, each producing its own triad of powers, until the inmost Divine reaches the soul leaving the body and clothes it with the garments of light.
reading:
This chapter sets out one continuous spiritual descent. There are five Fathers, but they are not five Gods; they are the one Lord in five discrete degrees of accommodation, each called forth from the one above. The teaching's whole point is that the Divine Esse cannot reach the soul directly but must clothe itself in successive states, each of which produces its own threefold operation, until at the last degree the Lord meets the regenerate human at the threshold of heaven.

The First Father is the Father of Greatness himself — the Lord in his inmost Divine, the unmeasured, the glorious, the only-begotten First, who exists before all things and out of whom all things come. From him emanate three: the Great Spirit (the Mother of Life, Divine Wisdom in her bringing-forth), the Beloved of the Lights (Divine Love in its emanating dearness), and a third — the Ambassador-power. These are not three subordinate gods but the first articulation of love, wisdom, and the proceeding into operation. By them Darkness is humbled and its pride-of-heart laid waste, and kingship is established in the aeons. This is the inmost movement of the Divine: the moment Divine Esse becomes Divine Existere by polarising into love and its proceeding wisdom, and the proprium is at once put under judgment.

The Second Father is the Third Ambassador — the Protomē, the foremost figure of the King of the Lights. He is Divine Truth in its revealing, awakening operation. From him also proceed three powers, but now the descent is one degree lower: the Pillar of Glory (the Perfect Man / Omophoros, who bears upward all things — the axis of return that supports the natural cosmos), Jesus the Radiance (through whom eternal life is given), and the Virgin of Light, the Sophia, who by her image steals the heart of the aeons and Powers from the pride-of-heart of the natural greatness. At this second Father the Lord's emanation is no longer the inner self-articulation of the Divine but its turning-toward-creation: a column of bearing, a radiance of life, and a pure receptivity by which higher beings are drawn back from self-exaltation.

The Third Father is Jesus the Radiance — the same power named in the second triad, now standing as a Father in his own right because he repeats, at a lower degree, what the Second Father did. Pointedly, the text says he calls "three callings, after the likeness of the Second Father": each Father mirrors the one above. His three are the Mind of Light (illumined rational understanding), the Judge whose tabernacle is established in the air under the wheel of the stars (Divine Truth in its judicial discrimination over the natural mind, set above the cyclic course of natural states), and a third with two faces in his countenance, gazing toward the heaven the Father established — bearing the Call and the Hearing, standing before his Father the King of Honor, and saying: "I am the one who has seen him with my Father; what you have seen is what you do." Here the descent has reached the level at which Divine Truth becomes redemptive in the natural: rational illumination above, judgment in the middle, and the bi-faced messenger below who unites Call and Hearing and delivers what has been seen as what must be done. Vision becomes obedience; the heavenly pattern becomes earthly act.

The Fourth Father is the Mind of Light, again named one degree down from the third triad. His powers are described as standing "in the likeness of Jesus," and the first of them is named: the Apostle — the Lord in his sending of revealed truth into the world. At this register, the descent has crossed into the human spiritual mind; the Divine now operates as illumined rational and as the apostolic word that reaches into the cosmos.

The Fifth and last Father is the Form of Light. This is the consummating degree, and the text describes it from the side of the soul: it is "revealed to everyone who comes forth from the body, into the likeness of the icon of the apostle." That is, when the regenerate soul leaves its natural body, what meets it is the very Form which the four prior Fathers have been descending toward. The Form of Light comes accompanied by three great glorious angels, mirroring once again the threefold pattern: one bears the prize in his right hand (the divine power of blessing and reward), the second bears the garment of light (the soul's clothing in confirmed external truth), the third holds the diadem, the wreath, and the crown of light (the ruling principle of conjunction by which the regenerate state is sealed). They are revealed through one another and recognised by those who recognise them — and by this recognition, some attain life forever and receive the garments of light given to the righteous, the men of peace and mercy.

Read as a whole, the teaching is a doctrine of discrete degrees of influx. The Lord cannot pour his inmost Divine straight into a human soul; the abyss between the unmeasured Father of Greatness and a single dying righteous person must be bridged by accommodations, each of which is itself fully Divine yet steps the descent down by one register. Five times the same threefold pattern repeats — emanation, mediation, manifestation — and at each step the same Divine Truth is named in a more outward form: Ambassador, Radiance, Mind, Apostle, Form. The triads are not different stories but the one operation of love-wisdom-effect refracted at each level. By the time the chain reaches the soul at the moment of bodily release, what arrives is the entire chain compressed into a Form that can be put on as garment, diadem, and crown. The teaching therefore explains, in cosmological language, the architecture by which regeneration is actually possible: the Lord meets the soul in ultimates only because he has first organized himself in five discrete degrees from the inmost outward, and the very figures who clothe the righteous at the end are the same who, at the beginning, humbled the Darkness.

major_images.meaning: The fullness of process — love, wisdom, and effect — refracted at every level of descent
